name: crosswalk
statement: Engram supplies evidence about how a memory control plane behaves: each row names a claim, the test in this repository that proves it, and an article of the EU AI Act or the GDPR the evidence bears on. A row never says that Engram, or a deployment using it, meets an obligation. Whether a deployment is compliant depends on its purpose, its operator and facts the plane cannot see.
method: After arXiv 2512.13907 (Buscemi et al., idea only; abstract read): each obligation is cut to the paragraph or point a memory plane can give evidence for, and each claim is tied to a verification activity this repository runs, a test named by file and title. The structure is borrowed, not the contents.

ai-act.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 June 2024 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
ai-act.amended_by: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), OJ L, 2026/1744, 24.7.2026, http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32026R1744, read 2026-11-21. Its amending provisions change the text of none of Articles 12, 13, 14, 15, 19 and 26 cited here. Its point (18) adds Article 42(3), under which high-risk AI systems within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 for which the conditions of its Article 12(1) hold are deemed to comply with the cybersecurity requirements set out in Article 15; that bears on rows AIA-15-1 and AIA-15-5. Its new Article 113, third paragraph, point (c) makes Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3, with the exception of Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 for high-risk systems under Article 6(2) and Annex III and from 2 August 2028 under Article 6(1) and Annex I.

gdpr.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (General Data Protection Regulation)
gdpr.amended_by: The text as published in the Official Journal; corrigenda were not read. No article number cited here is changed by a corrigendum the Publications Office lists for this act, which was not checked either.

obligations.heading: Record-keeping
obligations.quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.

obligations.heading: Record-keeping
obligations.quote: In order to ensure a level of traceability of the functioning of a high-risk AI system that is appropriate to the intended purpose of the system, logging capabilities shall enable the recording of events relevant for:

obligations.heading: Record-keeping
obligations.quote: identifying situations that may result in the high-risk AI system presenting a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1) or in a substantial modification;

obligations.heading: Record-keeping
obligations.quote: monitoring the operation of high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 26(5).

obligations.heading: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
obligations.quote: where applicable, the technical capabilities and characteristics of the high-risk AI system to provide information that is relevant to explain its output;

obligations.heading: Human oversight
obligations.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.

obligations.heading: Human oversight
obligations.quote: to correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output, taking into account, for example, the interpretation tools and methods available;

obligations.heading: Human oversight
obligations.quote: to decide, in any particular situation, not to use the high-risk AI system or to otherwise disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system;

obligations.heading: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.

obligations.heading: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
obligations.quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.

obligations.heading: Automatically generated logs
obligations.quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data.

obligations.heading: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
obligations.quote: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use

obligations.heading: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
obligations.quote: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months

obligations.heading: Principles relating to processing of personal data
obligations.quote: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed (‘data minimisation’);

obligations.heading: Principles relating to processing of personal data
obligations.quote: accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date; every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that personal data that are inaccurate, having regard to the purposes for which they are processed, are erased or rectified without delay (‘accuracy’);

obligations.heading: Principles relating to processing of personal data
obligations.quote: kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed;

obligations.heading: Principles relating to processing of personal data
obligations.quote: processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security of the personal data, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures (‘integrity and confidentiality’).

obligations.heading: Principles relating to processing of personal data
obligations.quote: The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with, paragraph 1 (‘accountability’).

obligations.heading: Conditions for consent
obligations.quote: Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data.

obligations.heading: Conditions for consent
obligations.quote: The data subject shall have the right to withdraw his or her consent at any time.

obligations.heading: Right to erasure (‘right to be forgotten’)
obligations.quote: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning him or her without undue delay and the controller shall have the obligation to erase personal data without undue delay where one of the following grounds applies:

obligations.heading: Responsibility of the controller
obligations.quote: the controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and to be able to demonstrate that processing is performed in accordance with this Regulation.

obligations.heading: Data protection by design and by default
obligations.quote: both at the time of the determination of the means for processing and at the time of the processing itself, implement appropriate technical and organisational measures

obligations.heading: Data protection by design and by default
obligations.quote: That obligation applies to the amount of personal data collected, the extent of their processing, the period of their storage and their accessibility. In particular, such measures shall ensure that by default personal data are not made accessible without the individual's intervention to an indefinite number of natural persons.

obligations.heading: Records of processing activities
obligations.quote: where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data;

obligations.heading: Security of processing
obligations.quote: the ability to ensure the ongoing confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services;

obligations.heading: Security of processing
obligations.quote: a process for regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organisational measures for ensuring the security of the processing.

claims.claim: No read returns an item whose scope matrix or grants exclude the reader.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (What this is; make test-invariants); docs/architecture.md (invariant 1); docs/conventions/testing.md

tests.it: invariant 1: no read returns an item the actor's scope and grants exclude
a cross-scope read is denied and the explanation lists the filtered-out count

claims.limits: The actor is self-asserted on every surface (ADR 0027): the filter holds for the identity a surface declares, not for an authenticated person.

obligations.why: the read filter is a technical measure against unauthorised processing of memory content
accessibility by default is limited to the scopes a reader belongs to and the grants that name it
evidence for the confidentiality of what a reader is given

claims.claim: No write lands in a scope whose policy forbids its class or its source.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (What this is); docs/architecture.md (invariant 2); docs/conventions/testing.md; ADR 0007

tests.it: invariant 2: no write lands in a scope whose policy forbids its class or source
denies a forbidden-class write without calling the adapter, with one event

claims.limits: Holds for writes that cross the plane; a write made to the store outside it is the no-bypass rows' concern (C34, C35). Within what a rule admits, a co-member less trusted than an item's owner may rewrite, retire or evict that item (packages/core/test/counterexamples/trust.test.ts, GH-38; card E2.11 is the opt-in fix).

obligations.why: the write gate is a deterministic defence against a third party altering what the system later reads (memory poisoning)
protection against unauthorised processing at the point content enters memory
evidence for the integrity of what memory holds

claims.claim: Every read or write appends exactly one event, and every denial carries a reason and a policy id.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (What this is; rule 3); docs/conventions/testing.md (invariant 3); ADR 0007 (decision D6)

tests.it: invariant 3: every read or write appends exactly one event, and a denial carries a reason and a policy id

describe: Plane.write: every outcome is an event (decision D6)
tests.it: an adapter that throws after an allow leaves one store-failure event, and rethrows

claims.limits: The log is not tamper-evident: no hash chain or signature protects it yet (ADR 0038 decides one; card E1.6 builds it).

obligations.why: every decision of the plane is recorded automatically as an event
each denial names the rule and the reason, which is how a risky write or read is identified afterwards
a controller can show from the log what was decided and under which rule
the per-decision record is material for demonstrating that processing followed the policy

claims.claim: Replaying the events of any write sequence gives the same state, store and read results: the log is the source of truth.

tests.it: invariant 4: replaying the events of any write sequence gives the same state, store and reads
rebuild equals incremental for any event sequence
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

obligations.why: the functioning of the plane can be traced, and reconstructed, from its events alone
a past state of memory can be shown from the log, not only asserted

claims.claim: After any write sequence no scope holds more active items of a class than its budget; every retire or evict event carries a reason and a policy id, and replay reproduces them.

tests.it: invariant 5: after any write sequence no scope holds more active items of a class than its budget, every retire or evict event carries a reason and a policy id, and replay reproduces them

describe: acceptance (card E2.4): budget exceeded evicts per policy; events recorded
tests.it: recency: the write that goes over evicts the oldest, in the same call

claims.limits: The budgets are the operator's policy values; the preset numbers are proposed values (ADR 0025).

obligations.why: a budget bounds how much a scope holds active of each class; in tension as C26 is, since an evicted item is retired, not deleted, and the store keeps it
the amount of data kept active by default is set by policy and enforced on every write

claims.claim: Adoption of what a store already holds never records a provenance kind more trusted than the plane holds for the item's id.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (make test-invariants); docs/conventions/testing.md (invariant 6); ADR 0004 (card RV4); docs/dogfood.md (limit 4)

tests.it: invariant 6: adoption never records a provenance kind more trusted than the plane holds for the item's id

obligations.why: editing a store record outside the plane cannot raise agent-written content to trusted content
evidence for the integrity of provenance across edits made outside the plane

claims.claim: Adoption never records a grant the plane does not hold for the item's id, so a grant typed into a store record does nothing.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (make test-invariants); docs/conventions/testing.md (invariant 7); ADR 0007 (card RV4); docs/dogfood.md (limit 4)

tests.it: invariant 7: adoption never records a grant the plane does not hold for the item's id

obligations.why: an item is not made readable to others by an edit nobody decided through the plane
where a deployment rests sharing on consent, a grant on record is one its owner made through the plane, not one written into a file

claims.claim: Across two handles over one log, with an offboarding among their operations, no reader gets an erased item back and the store holds the projection, whatever the interleaving.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (make test-invariants); ADR 0007 (card E2.6); ADR 0010 (card E2.6)

tests.it: invariant 1 across two handles: no reader gets an erased item back, and the store holds the projection, whatever the interleaving
a write under an erased id is refused, and the refusal names the erased scope only to its members
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

claims.limits: A promotion or derived write into a team or role scope that crashes after its bytes land and after the sweep can stay dormant in that store (ADR 0010, verification pass 4).

obligations.why: an erasure is not undone by a concurrent writer on another process
evidence for integrity under concurrent access to one log

claims.claim: Every recall can be explained: each item a read returns carries its score components, rank, admitting rule, grants used and validity window.
claims.source: AGENTS.md (What this is; What not to do); docs/architecture.md (read path); ADR 0009

tests.it: explains each item with rank, components, admitting rule, grants and validity
returns the explanations persisted for that read, in rank order

claims.limits: The explanation says why an item was admitted and how it ranked, not why a model acted on it.

obligations.why: the plane can give information relevant to explaining what memory it supplied
an overseer can read why each recalled item was given to the model

claims.claim: Explanations of a read are returned only to the actor who made it.

tests.it: refuses another actor's read, revealing none of its explanations (finding R5-12)
refuses another actor's read id in explain

obligations.why: an explanation names items and scores, so it is withheld from anyone but the reader
confidentiality of the audit trail of a read

claims.claim: A read reveals nothing about items out of the reader's reach; the read event, the audit record, keeps the full counts.
claims.source: docs/architecture.md (read path); ADR 0009 (decision D5, finding N1)

describe: reads reveal nothing about unreachable items (decision D5)
tests.it: a read's items, explanations, scores and filtered count ignore unreachable items

describe: Plane.read reveals nothing about items the reader cannot reach (decision D5)
tests.it: the read event, the audit record, keeps the full counts

obligations.why: no side channel of a read discloses another scope's items
unreachable items stay inaccessible by default, counts and ranks included
the event keeps what the reader is not shown, so the log stays complete

claims.claim: The plane, not the caller, sets an item's provenance from the source the harness gives the actor.

describe: Plane.write: the plane sets provenance (decision D4, finding R5-6)
tests.it: a harness-set source overrides the kind and actor the caller claims
labels a write model even when the launch actor carries source user (R3-5)

claims.limits: A write whose actor names no source keeps the kind and actor its caller claims, and the event's reason says so; packages/core/test/counterexamples/trust.test.ts (GH-39) pins this, including a sourceless write claiming user into team scope, which is allowed.

obligations.why: each event records where its content came from as the system saw it, not as a model claimed
a model cannot raise its own content's trust by claiming another source

claims.claim: Model, compaction and external content cannot leave person scope without a gate pass, and carries no grants.
claims.source: ADR 0004; ADR 0007; ADR 0021 (decision D4); docs/architecture.md (write path)

tests.it: denies model content outside person scope under the source-isolation rule
denies external content outside person scope even when the rule lists external

describe: acceptance (card E2.5): a widening is judged as a write into the target
tests.it: model-written content stays in person scope, however reviewed

describe: a grant change the gate refuses is one deny event, and nothing changes
tests.it: model content carries no grants

claims.limits: No surface labels content external yet (ADR 0004, schema version 1). Content is model content only as a harness labels it: a sourceless write claiming user is judged as user (C12; packages/core/test/counterexamples/trust.test.ts, GH-39).

obligations.why: untrusted content cannot spread to shared scopes, which limits a poisoning to the person it reached
agent-written content is not made accessible to others by default

claims.claim: The store is never written without an event: a store failure after an allow appends a deny event and rethrows.

describe: Plane.write: every outcome is an event (decision D6)
tests.it: a ref from another adapter is a store failure: one event, nothing projected
a store failure after the gate allowed is one deny event, and the call throws

obligations.why: a failed store call is recorded as well as a successful one
the log and the store do not silently diverge

claims.claim: Writers on different handles over one log are ordered by the log's lock: a decision made stale by another process is refused with its own event, and a committed grant removal stands.

describe: a committed decision on another handle
tests.it: R5: a grant change held while another grant change commits is refused, and the store holds the projection
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

describe: a committed decision on another handle
tests.it: R4: a handover held at its store write while the owner removes a grant keeps the removal and hands over the new version
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

describe: a committed decision on another handle
tests.it: R8: the conflict's deny event carries a reason and a policy id, no item, and is not shown to the grantee
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

obligations.why: integrity of memory under two processes sharing one log
where a deployment rests sharing on consent, a withdrawn grant is not brought back by a concurrent writer

claims.claim: Validity is bi-temporal: a read judges validity windows at its valid_at time and access at its own time, never before the log's head, so a past time cannot reopen an expired grant.

tests.it: cannot bring back what a grant's expiry closed at the read's time
excludes an item outside its validity window at the query time, and counts it

describe: RV-CORE-3: an access decision is never judged before the log's head
tests.it: a read named at a time before the last read cannot reopen an expired grant (the review's repro)

claims.limits: Writes, promotions and grant changes take the time a surface gives them; only the server's clock bounds them (ADR 0027).

obligations.why: a superseded or no longer valid fact is not served as current
a backdated read cannot regain access that has ended

claims.claim: Grants are explicit, scoped by class, and expire: a grant to everyone, to a bare wildcard, or without a class or an expiry is denied, and an expired grant admits nothing.

tests.it: denies a grant to everyone or to a bare kind wildcard
denies a grant without a class or without an expiry

describe: acceptance (card E9.4): a grant change is recorded as an event
tests.it: a grant expires: the read filter stops honouring it with no further event
does not admit through a grant for another class

claims.limits: The read filter still honours a grant without class or expiry on an item that never passed the gate (ADR 0021, decision D4); no maximum expiry is set (ADR 0034, open question).

obligations.why: a grant cannot make an item accessible to an indefinite number of persons
where a deployment rests sharing on consent, each grant on record names whom, which class and until when the owner allowed; a grant is not itself the data subject's consent

claims.claim: Only the item's owner, user-sourced and a member of its scope, changes its grants, and each change is one update event.
claims.source: docs/architecture.md (grant changes); docs/dogfood.md (what a zero cannot show)

tests.it: a grant change is one update event and lands exactly when the oracle permits it

describe: a grant change the gate refuses is one deny event, and nothing changes
tests.it: a member who is not the owner may not change the grants

describe: a grant change the gate refuses is one deny event, and nothing changes
tests.it: an agent acting for the owner may not change the grants

claims.limits: Identity and source are self-asserted (ADR 0027): the owner's agent posting as the owner with source user reads exactly as the owner, a blind spot the dogfood report's tests name. A first write may carry grants, and with no source its claimed kind stands (packages/core/test/counterexamples/trust.test.ts, GH-39); this row is about changing the grants of an item that exists.

obligations.why: where a deployment rests sharing on consent, a grant on record is an act of the item's owner, logged as one event

claims.claim: Removing a grant is one event, after which the grantee reads nothing through it.

describe: acceptance (card E9.4): a grant change is recorded as an event
tests.it: the owner removes it: a second update event, and the grantee reads nothing

claims.limits: What the grantee already read stays wherever its harness keeps it, such as Claude Code's transcripts (docs/dogfood.md, limit 7).

obligations.why: where a deployment rests sharing on consent, withdrawal is one act of the owner, as simple as the grant, and takes effect on the next read

claims.claim: A person scope is never readable by others without a live grant, and a role context never reads a person scope.

describe: acceptance (card E9.2): a cross-person read is denied in the fixture
tests.it: Sam, a teammate, sees nothing of Dana's person scope without a live grant

describe: acceptance (card E9.2): the twin profile loads
tests.it: a role context never reads a person scope, and a role takes no personal classes or sources

obligations.why: by default a person's memory is accessible to nobody else without that person's grant

claims.claim: Offboarding hands each role scope the leaver holds to a successor, one update event per item.

describe: acceptance (card E9.7): offboarding Dana, Sam succeeds her in role:lead
tests.it: the successor reads the role items, and they are his

claims.unmapped: continuity of role memory is an organisational property; no article of either act cited here asks for it

claims.claim: Offboarding erases the person scope: its items leave the store and the projection, their content is redacted in the log, replay honours the erasure, and a deletion report names by id what was done and what it cannot reach.

describe: acceptance (card E9.7): offboarding Dana, Sam succeeds her in role:lead
tests.it: the person items are gone from the store and the index, and stay gone

describe: acceptance (card E9.7): offboarding Dana, Sam succeeds her in role:lead
tests.it: the deletion report names what was done and what it cannot reach, by id only
the projection rebuilt from the log equals the incremental one

claims.limits: The erasure does not reach a store's own history (Letta's git), pi session files that mirrored the events, backups, or a harness's transcripts; for a record a store refuses to delete, the log keeps a merging content hash, which short content can be guessed from (ADR 0010).

obligations.why: the plane's means of erasing a person's memory, store and log included
the deletion report records what was erased and what was out of reach
the redaction keeps each event, its decision and reason, and removes only the content, which is where the six-month log keeping gives way to data protection law

claims.claim: An erased item does not come back: a write or a store record under an erased id is refused and deleted, and erased content left in a store is refused in that scope under any id.
claims.source: ADR 0010 (cards E2.6 and RV4); docs/dogfood.md (setup, step 3)

tests.it: a record under an erased id that reappears in the store (a write that was in flight, a restored copy) is never adopted, and deleted
tests.enclosed: forEachBackend (packages/core/test/db/backends.ts) loops over the backends and runs the block in one describe per backend; the SQLite describe has no skip condition, so the test runs

describe: offboarding a person whose memory is an adopted Claude Code folder
tests.it: erases the imported items, names the files left in the folder, and re-adoption brings none back

describe: offboarding a person whose memory is an adopted Claude Code folder
tests.it: a case, width or invisible-character edit of an erased file is still refused

claims.limits: A Claude Code memory file left in the store is adopted again once its content changes in any way (ADR 0010, open question).

obligations.why: erased data is not reinstated by a later write, a restored copy or a moved folder

claims.claim: Lint evidence about an erased item is redacted from every lint event, keeping the lint id, severity and rule.

describe: lint evidence about an erased item
tests.it: is redacted from every lint event, keeping the lint id, severity and rule

obligations.why: the erasure reaches derived records about the item, not only the item

claims.claim: Only a user-sourced member of the person scope may offboard it; an agent is refused with one deny event.

tests.it: an agent cannot: one deny event and nothing changes

claims.limits: Without authentication this holds as far as the machine does (ADR 0027).

obligations.why: the one irreversible operation is reserved to a person
an agent cannot destroy memory it was not given the right to erase

claims.claim: Retention never deletes: a budget eviction or an expiry retires the item by event, and the store keeps its bytes.

describe: acceptance (card E2.4): budget exceeded evicts per policy; events recorded
tests.it: recency: the write that goes over evicts the oldest, in the same call
retain retires expired items with op retire, then the budget, and reports both

claims.limits: Both tests assert, past their titles, that the store still holds the retired item's bytes: the eviction's and the expiry's. Deletion of content happens only by erasure (C22).

obligations.why: retired items stay replayable, so the record of what memory held is kept
in tension: retiring keeps the content stored, so storage limitation rests on erasure and on the operator's choice of ttls

claims.claim: An item past its ttl is excluded at read before any sweep, and a sweep then retires it with op retire.

tests.it: an expired item is excluded at read before any sweep, counted in filtered
retain retires expired items with op retire, then the budget, and reports both

claims.limits: A sweep retires by ttl only in the actor's own person scope or for a user-sourced actor (ADR 0025, P4-6), so expired shared items are unreadable but not retired until a person sweeps.

obligations.why: an item is not used beyond the period the policy sets for its class and scope; in tension as C26 is, since expiry retires the item and the store keeps it
in tension: the ttl a policy sets per class and scope is a stated time limit, but it retires the item and keeps its bytes (C26), so it is a limit on use, not on erasure

claims.claim: A manual eviction rule evicts nothing and asks a person, as one evict event with decision ask.

describe: acceptance (card E2.4): budget exceeded evicts per policy; events recorded
tests.it: manual: nothing is evicted, one evict event with decision ask names the overage

obligations.why: the decision of what to forget is left to a natural person where the policy says so
the person decides instead of the system

claims.claim: A model, compaction or tool write restating content retired in its scope is denied.

tests.it: a model source restating retired content is denied, normalised
a compaction source restating retired content is denied, normalised
a tool source restating retired content is denied, normalised

claims.limits: Exact match after normalisation only; a paraphrase passes (ADR 0018).

obligations.why: an agent cannot relearn what retention or review removed by restating it

claims.claim: A retired item can be reinstated by an allowed update event.
claims.gap: no Plane method or surface reinstates an item yet (ADR 0025, decision 6 names a follow-up card), and no test exercises a reinstatement

obligations.why: reinstatement would let a person reverse an eviction the system made

claims.claim: Every lint finding is one lint event carrying the lint, severity and evidence, and every deterministic lint has a flag fixture and a near-miss fixture.

tests.it: records each finding as one lint event whose reason carries the lint, severity and evidence
has a flag and a near-miss fixture for every deterministic lint

obligations.why: a finding about memory quality is recorded as an event that names its evidence
lint events are recorded events relevant to monitoring the operation of the system
lint events are material a deployer's monitoring can read

claims.claim: Stale memory is flagged: the expired-validity lint flags an item past its window or ttl, and the source-changed lint an item whose source no longer hashes to what it recorded.

tests.it: flags an active item whose valid_to is not after the lint time
flags an item whose source now hashes to something else

claims.limits: A lint flags; it does not correct. The expired-validity lint is reliable only on keyed items (ADR 0005).

obligations.why: a step towards finding memory that is no longer accurate or up to date

claims.claim: Model-based lints run only through an injected ModelCall, record each finding with its usage, and leave the log as it was when a call fails.

tests.it: without a lint model the model lints do not run and the report has no judgments
